title: Neural and bioelectric patterning networks may share dynamics

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Neural and bioelectric patterning networks may share dynamics

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because non-neuronal cells use many of the same ion-channel and electrical-synapse mechanisms as neurons for pattern formation and repair, significant commonalities may exist between the dynamics of neural networks and of bioelectric signalling networks that control shape, so neural modelling tools such as dynamic causal modelling may apply to morphogenesis data.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Conclusion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This suggests the possibility that significant commonalities may exist between the dynamics of neural networks and of bioelectric signalling networks that control shape determination [20,21,83].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Conclusion”. Scope: Non-neural tissues with bioelectric signalling during development and regeneration

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction can be operationalized by comparative system identification, but available models and datasets cover only selected systems and often lack matched perturbations. They can test limited commonalities rather than the broad claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit matched dynamical model classes to neural and non-neural bioelectric time series and compare inferred coupling, attractors, and perturbation responses using preregistered similarity metrics. Shared predictive structure beyond generic nonlinear dynamics would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Common ion-channel components do not by themselves establish common network dynamics.

Public non-neural voltage time series with anatomical outcomes are sparse.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.3
data existence: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Neural recordings and DCM software are public, so one side of the proposed comparison can be prepared. The claim is about dynamics shared with bioelectric patterning networks, and those tissue voltage time series are not in an open dataset. Until they are, the comparison cannot be run.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit the same dynamic-causal-model class to neural time series and to time-resolved bioelectric recordings from non-neural tissue during patterning, then compare model evidence. Shared structure that beats unstructured alternatives would support the proposed commonality; a systematic failure on morphogenesis recordings would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Significant commonality is not given a numerical model-comparison threshold.

Public morphogenesis voltage time series with the sampling DCM needs are not deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.38
data existence: 0.32
data adequacy: 0.22
discriminating power: 0.28
